passage: I am Jahnavi, and I share a hostel lounge with Akash. On Tuesday I watched his phone light up three times, showing the name Rohan. Each time Akash turned the phone face down and stared at the TV. I could not tell whether he was angry or embarrassed; his ears were red, that I noticed. The fourth time I said, "That's a lot of calls." He said quietly, "I borrowed some money from him. I can't pay all of it yet and I don't know what to say." I said, "Tell him honestly what you can pay and when." He stepped into the corridor and called back. When he came in, he let out a long breath. "He said thanks for telling him," Akash said, looking a little lighter.

qa.q: How many times did Akash's phone light up before Jahnavi spoke?
qa.a: It lit up three times, and Jahnavi spoke after the fourth.

qa.q: What might Akash have been feeling when he turned the phone face down, and how sure can Jahnavi be?
qa.a: He was probably embarrassed about the debt, as his red ears and his later words suggest. Jahnavi says she could not tell for sure whether it was anger or embarrassment.

qa.q: What could Akash do to keep the friendship steady?
qa.a: He can keep his word on the amount and date he promised Rohan, and tell Rohan early if anything changes.

qa.q: How might Rohan see Akash's missed calls and then his honest call?
qa.a: Rohan probably wondered about the silence, and thanked Akash for telling him, which suggests honesty mattered more to him than the delay.

grounding: The protagonist borrowed from a friend and dodges calls out of embarrassment, then calls back and tells him honestly what he can pay.
